Hi everyone! I'm Frankie. I've been working on a formalization of
quadratic number fields in Lean 4 and am now upstreaming parts of it
to mathlib.
Current PRs:

  • #36347: Defines ℚ(√d) as a quadratic number field over ℚ, including
    the IsQuadraticField predicate, field/number field instances, and
    basic operations (trace, norm).

  • #36387 (depends on #36347): Proves parameter uniqueness — every quadratic
    field can be normalized to a squarefree integer parameter, and this
    parameter is unique.
    Upstream project: https://github.com/FrankieeW/QuadraticNumberFields
    The project is a fairly complete formalization covering:

  • Ring of integers classification: the main theorem that
    d % 4 ≠ 1 → 𝒪 ≃ ℤ[√d] and d % 4 = 1 → 𝒪 ≃ ℤ[(1+√d)/2]

  • Discriminant: Δ = d if d ≡ 1 mod 4, else Δ = 4d

  • Totally real / totally complex / CM classification:
    d > 0 → totally real, d < 0 → totally complex & CM field

  • Norm: multiplicativity, unit characterization (N(α) = ±1)

  • Dedekind domain: ℤ[√d] is Dedekind iff d % 4 ≠ 1
  • Concrete examples for ℤ[√-5]: ideal factorization
    ((2) = (2,1+√-5)², (3) = (3,1+√-5)·(3,1-√-5)),
    ramification/inertia degrees, prime ideal verification
    The upstream project is also actively being developed, and I plan to
    continue upstreaming more results in follow-up PRs. Happy to address
    any review feedback!

Snir Broshi said:

#ItaLean 2025 > Projects: Quadratic Integers
https://pitmonticone.github.io/QuadraticIntegers/

Thanks for pointing this out! I wasn't aware of this project before.
It looks like it already has a very well-developed blueprint — I'll take a closer look.
You can see here for the final version (about the ring of integers).
Note that this was a project for beginners, so not everything is in full generality.

I have a modelling question about the d % 4 ≠ 1 case.

For the d % 4 = 1 case there seems to be no issue: one can model
ℤ[(1+√d)/2] using

abbrev ZOnePlusSqrtOverTwo (d : ℤ) : Type := QuadraticAlgebra ℤ d 1.

The difficulty arises in the other case (d % 4 ≠ 1), where the ring of
integers is ℤ[√d]. In mathlib this is represented by the type
Zsqrtd, which historically predates QuadraticAlgebra.

Conceptually this corresponds to the quadratic algebra
QuadraticAlgebra ℤ d 0. My current approach is therefore to treat
QuadraticAlgebra ℤ d 0 as the algebraic model and then connect it to
the existing objects via explicit ring isomorphisms:

QuadraticAlgebra ℤ d 0 ≃+* Zsqrtd d

and

𝓞 (Q(√d)) ≃+* QuadraticAlgebra ℤ d 0.

So the idea is to identify the ring of integers with
QuadraticAlgebra ℤ d 0, and then relate this to the existing Zsqrtd
type through a separate isomorphism.

Does this seem like a reasonable approach, given that Zsqrtd
historically predates QuadraticAlgebra?

More generally, would there be any motivation to refactor Zsqrtd
itself so that it is defined in terms of QuadraticAlgebra, or is it
preferable to keep the current separation and just relate them via
isomorphisms?
I may be wrong, but I would personally avoid Zsqrtd and would do everything for QuadraticAlgebra.

I also had the impression that in the long term it might make sense to base everything on QuadraticAlgebra rather than Zsqrtd.
My thought was that this might eventually require refactoring Zsqrtd itself, but that seems like a separate and potentially quite large piece of work.
I think there was discussion about replacing Zsqrtd with an abbrev for QuadraticAlgebra
Certainly that should be a standalone PR, but I would expect it to be quite simple

As Filippo A. E. Nuccio mentioned, I am also interested in quadratic fields since I need several results about quadratic fields for my work on the Kronecker–Weber theorem. I started working at the level of QuadraticAlgebra R a b:

  • #42207: the trace, with the relation z ^ 2 = trace z • z - algebraMap _ _ (norm z);
  • #42209: the change of generator ω ↦ u • ω + k as map/mapEquiv (for non-invertible u, this is the inclusion of the order of conductor u);
  • #42206: the discriminant and the classification of quadratic algebra.
• #42272: the degenerate cases over a field.
